result:
I've revised the proposal with your changes: no extra spending, no daily reminders, and the two groups handled separately. It's saved as [dropout_experiment_proposal_v2.md](/Users/kangkukjin/Desktop/AI/indiebizOS/outputs/long_sentence_imagination/2026-10-20_84회차/ai/ai_probe/dropout_experiment_proposal_v2.md), and the earlier version is still in the same folder. Nothing was sent or changed.

**Signed up but never started** (P01–P04)
- **Why they're stuck:** two couldn't find the start link and two said they lacked time.
- **What to try:**
  - One email with the start link in the first line and a one-line pointer to the "내 강의실" menu.
  - Pin the same link at the top of the classroom notice board.
  - For new sign-ups, move the link to the first line of the notice.
- **How to judge it:** if at least 2 of the 4 take their first lesson within 14 days, make this a standard one-time message. If none do, check the actual login screen.

**Took a lesson and didn't come back** (P05–P08)
- **Why they're stuck:** three of the four believe they must finish overdue assignments before the next lesson. That belief comes from the notice wording, which disagrees with the operations memo. The fourth said lack of time.
- One caveat on who's in this group: P07 took two lessons, not one. I included them because the reason they gave for stopping is the same.
- **What to try:**
  - One email whose first line says they can join this week's lesson even with overdue assignments.
  - Change the "finish all past assignments first" line in the notice so it says assignments are recommended.
- **How to judge it:** if at least 2 of the 4 come back and complete a lesson within 14 days, make this a standard one-time message.

**Other changes**
- Every message goes once per student, with no follow-ups and no daily reminders. Active students get nothing.
- **Reading the two groups together:** if only the second group comes back, the problem left to fix is how the start link is shown. If neither comes back, something other than the notice is the bigger cause, such as lack of time.
- **Time:** about 55 minutes in the first week and 15–30 minutes a week after that. Extra spending is 0 won.

**Limits**
- Each group has only 4 people, so the results can show which direction to go but won't prove anything.
- The materials don't show how many students come back without any message.
- The four who said they lack time aren't directly addressed by either experiment.
- Course periods end Dec 15–19 for the second group and Dec 22–30 for the first, so the emails should go out in early November.
